name: level3-playthrough-ecology
description: Level 3 (Treranium Depths) ecological shutdown scenario: massive krackle and obliviax blasts with no mitigation, long tick cycles to trigger ecology collapse. `campaign start level:treranium_depths` fails outright (tier-3, locked by default -- pre-existing, already documented per Finding #24 in this file's own step descriptions and Finding #58/#59 elsewhere in this doc); runs against the substitute new_game world instead. #553 (drill_hole became a queued, vehicle-gated action) breaks the rest of the named premise for real, not just the depth-mismatch Finding #61 already covered: this file's 6 patterns (5x4/4x5/5x5/5x5/6x5/6x6, 156 holes total -- the largest drilling total of any file in this batch) used to write every hole into state.drillHoles in one frame; now each hole is a queued drill_hole action a licensed driller spends real ticks physically driving a drill_rig to sink, one at a time, before charging/sequencing/blasting (unchanged, still operate on state.drillHoles only) can touch it. staffed:true's own composition costs real ticks too -- five employees and four vehicles' payroll/maintenance/fuel accrue whether or not they ever work. Under those costs, against a starting budget that tops out at $92,800 (staffed:true's free $50,000, plus $42,800 scrapping the debris_hauler/rock_digger/rock_fragmenter this blast-only file never uses) with zero income anywhere in the file (no contracts, ever), this pass measured -- exhaustively, across paired vs. single drill_rig crews, immediate vs. deferred hiring, with and without the fleet scrap, with and without a relocate-before-blast maneuver that saves the rig from its own blast -- that the mine cannot survive past its first blast's aftermath. BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS (100, Bankruptcy.ts) always runs out before a second pattern can be drilled with a single-driller pace this budget can afford, let alone before three more patterns' worth of blasts (900+ ticks, the pre-#553 file's own requirement to first push ecology to 0) could ever fire. The result: pattern 1 drills and blasts for real (20 holes, krackle, single-driller, with the 7 hand-hires deferred to after drilling for cash reasons; 11 of 12 employees die; ecology crashes 50 -> 29.53; the drill_rig survives a deliberate relocate before firing). Pattern 2 orders its 20 holes for free but never drills a single one -- no licensed, equipped driller survives the budget to work it. Patterns 3-6 are never reached at all: continuing to narrate drill_plan cycles nothing can ever staff past this crew/licensing dead end would document nothing real. levelEndReason never reaches 'ecological_shutdown' -- the named premise's ending no longer holds, exactly the class of finding Finding #24 already established elsewhere in this file (the named thing doesn't happen; here is what really does, re-measured and asserted exactly). #586-followup (this session's own fix, real interaction-mode CI failure): a prior pass of this file additionally carried ~100 ticks of dead post-drilling/post-hiring tick padding before pattern 1's own charge step (holes and the 7-employee hire were both already done by real tick 260, but the charge command wasn't issued until real tick 360, sandbox-confirmed) -- long enough that it ate directly into BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS's margin and flipped levelEnded/levelEndReason to 'bankruptcy' *during pattern 1's own charge wait*, before its `sequence`/`blast` steps ever ran. That is what the interaction-mode click failure on `#bs-blast-panel [data-field="delay-step"]` actually was -- the level-end overlay was already up, not a transient click race, and it stayed up (blocking every subsequent player-role click on the blast panel) for the rest of the file. Removing that dead padding lets charging finish at real tick 312 instead of 436, and the mine survives pattern 1's charge/sequence/blast for real: `levelEnded`/`levelEndReason`/`bankrupt` are false/null/false through the whole file now, not true/'bankruptcy'/true from partway through pattern 1 onward -- only pattern 2's own drill_plan-with-no-driller dead end (a crew/licensing limit, not a game-over state) still holds.

steps.description: #553: staffed:true's four vehicles all come unmanned (driverId:null) -- this crews the free drill_rig with the staffed driller (employee #1) before anything can drill. Panel opened once here; every later vehicle step in this file reuses it already open.

Finding: this file is pure blast-only (no contracts, no hauling, no rock clearing anywhere in it, per the pre-#553 pass's own note) -- the debris_hauler/rock_digger/rock_fragmenter staffed:true grants are dead weight the moment the game opens, and under #553 that weight is no longer free: drill_hole is now a queued action a driller spends real ticks on, and this file's 6 patterns (156 holes total, the largest in this batch) need a very long drilling window before their first blast can even fire. VEHICLE_SCRAP_RESIDUAL_FRACTION is 0.4 (balance.ts) and these three are still at full HP, so scrapping them back for $10,000 + $20,000 + $12,800 = $42,800 turns three idle maintenance drains into the cash cushion that keeps the mine solvent through that window -- explored and required; see the tick-block notes below for the arithmetic.
Same finding as the debris_hauler scrap above -- rock_digger never does anything in this file either.
Same finding -- rock_fragmenter is the third and last unused staffed vehicle; only the drill_rig (vehicle #1) is ever driven in this file.

campaign start level:treranium_depths FAILS at step 1 ("Level treranium_depths is locked. Complete previous levels first." -- Campaign.ts unlocks only tier-1 levels by default, treranium_depths is tier 3) -- a real, pre-existing scenario bug predating #553 (Finding #24), untouched by this pass. Every subsequent command runs against whatever the substitute new_game seed:3666 staffed:true produced instead of the intended level.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:5 cols:4 spacing:3 depth:6 diameter:0.089 start:10,10
steps.description: #553: confirming the grid only orders the 20 holes -- they are ghosts until a licensed driller drives the drill_rig to each one, so holeCount is 0 here (was 20 pre-#553); the tick blocks below drain the order.

expect.note: #553: sandbox-measured. A single driller (employee #1, the staffed:true composition's only driving.drill_rig licence) lands this 20-hole pattern in 13 tick(20)/event(choose 0) cycles -- 260 ticks -- interspersed with the fatigue-collapse rest cycles Employee.ts's needs system forces on a site with no living_quarters (a real driller collapses and rests in the dirt repeatedly, not just once). The 7 hand-hired employees below are NOT hired yet at this point -- deliberately: cash crosses BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD ($5,000, balance.ts) on its own well before this pattern finishes even with the scrap boost, and BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS is only 100 -- hiring 7 more salaries any earlier than this checkpoint burns the grace period before the first blast can even fire (sandbox-measured: hiring all 7 at tick 0 instead of here bankrupts the mine mid-pattern-1, around tick 220). Hiring here, once the single driller is already 16/20 holes in, is the latest point cash can still afford all seven ($20,138 vs. $8,300 total hiring cost) while leaving the rest of this pattern's drilling window inside the 100-tick grace once the new payroll starts compounding.

#553: this is the same 7-employee hand-hire this file has always done (driller x3, blaster x3, driver x1) -- only its position in the file moved, from immediately after `finances` to right here, mid-pattern-1. Renumbered #6-#12 now that staffed:true claims #1-#5. See the note on the tick(20) step 13 cycles up for why the timing had to move.

Corrected from role guard/command to role player/real clicks (a sibling file in this same batch, level1-playthrough-win.json, found the control this file's first pass missed): `move_here` is a real, player-clickable vehicle action -- select the vehicle, click MOVE HERE in the selection bar that opens (SelectionBar.ts's SelectionAction union) -- so there was never a genuine gap to guard against. The relocate itself is unchanged and still load-bearing: without it, the drill_rig that just finished sinking this pattern is still parked among the very holes about to detonate, and Damage.ts's fragment-hit check (BUILDING_DAMAGE_THRESHOLD 500 kJ, well below what a CATASTROPHIC-rated krackle blast throws at point-blank range) destroys it in the blast that follows -- sandbox-confirmed: skipping this step and firing immediately drops vehicleCount to 0 after the blast below, with no cash left anywhere in this file to buy a replacement rig. Moving the rig off to the side first -- even only 15 ticks' worth of travel at drill_rig's speed 1 (VEHICLE_BASE_STATS, balance.ts), well short of actually reaching (35,35) -- is enough separation that the same blast leaves it standing (sandbox-confirmed: vehicleCount stays 1). The 4 employees this blast kills below are unaffected either way; only the vehicle's survival depends on this step. #553-followup round 2 (issue #586 CI): the #553-followup round 1 fix (below, kept for history) swapped the Fleet-panel-row click for `clickEntity` (direct scene pick) reasoning that FleetPanel.update() only runs while its panel is visible and this file's vehicles panel had been superseded by the employees panel ~880 steps earlier. That diagnosis was real but incomplete, and the swap traded it for a second, worse bug: by this point in the file the drill_rig has just finished sinking all 20 holes and is parked at/near the last one, and BlastPlanOverlay keeps every drilled hole's marker geometry live and pickable (GameRenderer.showBlastPlanOverlay -- visible whenever any hole exists, independent of which panel is open, per src/renderer/GameRenderer.ts's `allHoles.length === 0` check). `clickEntity` aims the camera and clicks dead-center on the vehicle's own settled (x,z) -- which, with the rig sitting on top of a hole, lands the raycast on the hole marker's nearer geometry instead of the vehicle (sandbox-confirmed via run-all-scenarios' failure probe: the selection bar that opened only had a Focus action, the hole/fragment-only action set, never move_here/follow/haul/unassign). The three sibling files cited as precedent for clickEntity here (nav-move-costs-visual.json, vehicle-task-states-visual.json, nav-dynamic-updates-visual.json) all reach their move_here step with no blast plan overlay live, so they never hit this collision -- this file is the one place in the suite where a vehicle and a pickable hole marker coexist at the click point. The actual precedent for *this* failure mode is issue #512 (`vehicle-traffic.json`'s hauler #2/#3/#4 comments): "selected via its Fleet panel row instead of the scene raycast that could only ever hit [the wrong entity]" -- the Fleet panel row's click handler (`FleetPanel.ts`'s card listener -> `onSelectVehicleCb` -> `UIManager.setSelectVehicleHandler` -> `scenePicking.select()` in main.ts) calls `ScenePicking.select()` directly with the given id, never raycasting the scene at all, so it cannot collide with a hole marker or anything else. Restored that path here, with the one addition #553-followup round 1 was right about: an explicit `clickSelector` on `#bs-toolbar [data-panel="vehicles"]` immediately before the row click, so FleetPanel.update() actually runs and renders `[data-vehicle-id="1"]` before `waitForSelector` looks for it, regardless of how long the employees panel had been open instead. #553-followup round 3 (issue #586 CI, this time debugged against live browser state rather than more static reasoning): round 2's Fleet-panel-row click is structurally raycast-free and CI still failed with the identical "not in the DOM at all" symptom for `move_here` -- proving the bug was never about *how* the vehicle got selected. Replayed this file's exact command sequence through a standalone Puppeteer session against a live dev server up to this step and inspected `window.__gameConsole('vehicle list')`: `[1] drill_rig at (16,22) task: idle HP: 120 driver:none` -- the driller (employee #1, Gus Rubble) auto-dismounts the rig the instant its drilling task finishes, which flips FleetPanel.makeVehicleCard's driver row from the compact text-only `makeDriverRow` to the taller `makeAssignRow` (a real `<select>` + "Assign" button, fleetDetailSections.ts). `document.elementFromPoint()` at the exact center of `[data-vehicle-id="1"]`'s bounding box confirmed the center point now lands on that `<select>` -- and `FleetPanel.ts`'s own card click listener explicitly no-ops for `target.closest('button, select, input, a')`, by design (so a click meant for the assign dropdown doesn't also select the vehicle underneath). Puppeteer's `page.click(selector)` (what `clickSelector` uses) always clicks the center of the matched element's bounding box, so clicking the whole card silently swallowed the click and `onSelectVehicleCb` never fired -- no selection ever happened, hence no `#bs-selection-bar` and no `move_here` button anywhere in the DOM. Confirmed live in-browser: `document.querySelector('[data-vehicle-id="1"]').dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click'))` (bypassing the center-point ambiguity) opens the selection bar correctly with `move_here` present, and a real `page.click('[data-vehicle-id="1"]')` reproduces the failure exactly. This is correct, intentional FleetPanel behavior, not a source bug: a real player clicking dead-center of that same card, over the dropdown, would also open the dropdown rather than select the vehicle -- the scenario's click target was just imprecise once the card's content (and therefore its geometric center) changed shape after the driver dismounted. First retry aimed at `.bs-fleet-status` (the status chip in the card's head row, spatially clear of the assign row) instead of the whole card, and command mode/the unit test both stayed green, but interaction mode traded one race for another: `FleetPanel.refreshDynamic()` (`FleetPanel.ts`) replaces `.bs-fleet-status`/`.bs-fleet-hp`/`.bs-fleet-load` wholesale via `Element.replaceWith()` on every `update()` poll (every tick the panel is visible), so the exact DOM node Puppeteer resolved the selector to can be swapped out from under it between locating the element and dispatching the click -- CI's `element is present and looks clickable — the browser still refused it` (the catch-all `describeUnclickable` branch, `interaction-executor.ts`) is exactly that failure mode: `inspectSelector`'s own post-failure re-query sees a fresh, valid replacement node and finds nothing wrong with it. Fixed by targeting the card's head row (`> div:first-child`, `FleetPanel.makeVehicleCard`'s `head` div) instead: built once per `render()` and never touched by `refreshDynamic()`, so the node is stable across polls, and its own children (icon chip, name/type text, status chip, locate button) keep the head row's geometric center over the `nameCol` text -- fixed-width icon chip and fixed-width status-chip+locate-button bookend a `flex:1` name column that always claims the row's middle, well clear of both interactive controls at the edges and of the driver/assign row below.

expect.note: #586-followup (this session's own fix): tickCount dropped from 360 to 265 -- this session removed ~100 ticks of dead post-drilling/post-hiring tick padding earlier in this file (holes and the 7-employee hire were both already done by real tick 260, but the charge step wasn't issued until tick 360), the same class of interaction-mode CI fix as level1-win-efficient.json's pattern-1 padding removal. resolveEventIfPending added after this last tick batch (real CI finding: the charge step's own toolbar reopen click failed with 'covered by div.bs-confirm-overlay') -- command mode's own tick loop auto-resolves any pending random event every iteration (command-runner.ts), interaction mode's raw `tick 15` command does not, so a fatigue-collapse/random event spawned on the closing ticks of this batch could leave its dialog up (isPaused:true) blocking every subsequent toolbar click, same event-freeze asymmetry already fixed elsewhere in this batch (blast-execution-visual.json, level1-lose-ecology.json).

steps.description: Charge All commits the panel's current product card / amount / stemming (ChargeStep.chargeAll, Charge.ts): the krackle product card selects the explosive, 5 amount increments take 5 -> 10kg (krackle's maximum) and 5 stemming decrements take 2.0 -> 1.0m. #553-followup round 3 (issue #586 CI, second bug surfaced only once the move_here fix above let the run reach this far for the first time): the preceding step switches the active toolbar panel to Fleet to select the drill_rig, and this step never switched it back to Blast before clicking `[data-step="2"]` -- CI failed with `element has zero size (0x0)`, the same panel-still-on-a-different-tab symptom already diagnosed and fixed for blast-execution-visual.json's grids 2-4 in this same round (both bugs pre-date this specific investigation: b9367f6, #553's original landing commit, already had this exact gap, just never reached in interaction mode until move_here itself started working). Added the missing `#bs-toolbar [data-panel="blast"]` reopen click, matching that sibling fix.

#586-followup (this session's own fix, real interaction-mode CI failure): this step used to hard-assert `levelEnded:true, levelEndReason:'bankruptcy'` here, before pattern 1's own `sequence`/`blast` steps ever ran -- exactly what made the interaction-mode click on `#bs-blast-panel [data-step="3"]` (the `sequence` step below) fail with 'element is covered by div': the level-end overlay was already up, blocking every player-role click on the blast panel for the rest of pattern 1. Root cause: ~100 ticks of dead post-drilling/post-hiring tick padding earlier in this file (holes and the 7-employee hire were both already done by real tick 260, but the charge step wasn't issued until real tick 360) ate into BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS's margin for no reason -- removing that padding (see the tick-15 step's own note above) lets charging finish at real tick 312 instead of 436, comfortably before bankruptcy fires. `levelEnded`/`levelEndReason` corrected to false/null -- sandbox-confirmed the mine survives pattern 1's charge, sequence, and blast for real now.

Sequence's delay-step stepper carries data-field="delay-step" (Sequence.ts). 3 decrement clicks: 25ms default -> 20 -> 15 -> 10 (DELAY_STEP_INCREMENT=5ms, Sequence.ts). #586-followup: this was never actually a transient-overlay race -- the level-end overlay was permanently up by this point (see the wait_until step's own note above), and this session's padding fix keeps the level running past this step for real. awaitUsable is kept regardless, matching the pattern used elsewhere in this batch. `levelEnded`/`levelEndReason` corrected to false/null.

This blast fires for real (campaign start's lock, per the Finding above, only means it runs on the substitute new_game world, not that firing is blocked). #554: with charging now real, queued work, 47 more ticks elapse than the pre-#554 file needed. Finding (this pass, superseded by #557): all 12 employees die (deathCount 0 -> 12) -- a prior pass here read 11, with one hand-hired employee surviving as merely 'injured', but that reading depended on a Damage.ts bug (processProjections skipped any already-injured employee from every later fragment in the same blast, so a first, weaker graze made them immune to a subsequent, genuinely lethal one) that #557's fixer pass closed alongside the debris-attenuation work that exposed it -- widening hits from an exact 2m radius out to the full 15m BLAST_DANGER_MARGIN_M made a stray early graze-then-lethal-hit sequence, on the same employee within one blast, actually likely instead of a near-impossible coincidence. Ecology crashes 50 -> 29.53 (ScoreManager.ts's vibration-based ecology penalty, unchanged from the pre-#554 figure -- vibration is a function of the charge/pattern, not of who was standing nearby). The drill_rig (vehicle #1) survives too, thanks to the relocate step above. #586-followup: `levelEnded`/`levelEndReason` corrected to false/null -- this session's padding fix (see the wait_until step's own note above) means the mine is no longer bankrupt by the time this blast fires.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:4 cols:5 spacing:3 depth:6 diameter:0.089 start:25,10
steps.description: Finding #62 (this pass): ordering a plan is free and unrestricted -- drill_plan itself never checks cash or crew, so this still succeeds and queues 20 ghost holes exactly as declared. What changes is everything downstream: there is no licensed, equipped driller left -- the only driving.drill_rig licence on the roster died with employee #1 in the blast above, none of the 7 hand-hired employees hold it, and licensing one (`employee assign_skill <id> skill:driving.drill_rig level:1`) would not help even if it were free -- there is nothing left to spend on a second vehicle, and the one surviving rig has no living driver to claim it. orderedHoleCount sits at 20 forever; holeCount never leaves the 0 this pattern starts at. This is why this file only ever reaches 2 of its originally-described 6 patterns -- see the file description for the full finding. #586-followup: `levelEnded`/`levelEndReason` corrected to false/null -- the mine is no longer bankrupt (this session's padding fix, see the wait_until step's own note above), it simply has no driller left to work this second pattern.

Left as a command, guard role, and not reachable by any click sequence for a reason distinct from this file's earlier pre-#553 "invalid amount" findings (patterns 4/6, further down this file's own history): with holeCount at 0, the Drill step never has a single physically-drilled hole to hand off to Charge, so charge-all has nothing to act on and the panel's own step-advance leaves it unreachable -- there is no button a player could click through to a charge. The console has no such gate: createCharge (ChargePlan.ts) charges 0 of the 0 holes that exist, chargedCount stays 0, and the command itself reports success ("Charged 0 holes") rather than throwing.
Same gate as the charge step above -- with 0 drilled holes there is no Sequence tab content to click into. sequence auto reports "0 holes" and sequencedCount stays 0.

Left as a command: with nothing drilled, charged or sequenced there is no Fire step to reach, let alone execute. The command itself does not throw -- it produces a hollow, "BAD"-rated report (0 cleared voxels, 0 fragments, $0 ore value) and leaves every count at 0. No employee is anywhere near a blast that never really happens: deathCount and ecology are unchanged from the real blast above.

Finding #63 (this pass), rewritten for #554, then again for #586-followup: the file's real ending is no longer set here. #586-followup (this session's own fix): the pre-fix file's own ~100 ticks of dead post-drilling/post-hiring tick padding (see the `tick 15`/`wait_until` steps' own notes above) ate directly into BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS's margin, flipping levelEnded/levelEndReason to bankruptcy during pattern 1's own charge wait -- before its `sequence`/`blast` steps ever ran, which is what made a real interaction-mode click on the (by-then permanently covered) blast panel fail. Removing that padding lets charging finish at real tick 312 instead of 436, and the mine survives pattern 1's blast for real; this second pattern's own drill_plan (above) still can't be worked (no licensed driller survives the blast), but that is a crew/licensing dead end, not a game-over state. `cash` stays out of every remaining step's equality check for the same host-timing-sensitive reasons as the pre-#554 pass established (see the `move_here` step's own note) -- tick/hole/death/employee counts and level-end state stay exact.
No event pending at this checkpoint post-fix (sandbox-confirmed) -- kept as a no-op resolveEventIfPending for structural consistency with every other event choose 0 step in this file.
